# Rucirajātaka (Ja 275)

**ID:** Ja 275
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Rucirajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Splendid Crane
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja275

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rucirajātaka* (Ja 275), titled in English by Bhikkhu Sujato as *The Splendid Crane*, is a short birth-story belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. Delivered by the Buddha while staying at Jetavana, the discourse addresses a greedy monk (*lolabhikkhu*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. Rather than providing an independent prose narrative, the text references the story of the preceding *Lolajātaka* (Ja 274), presenting only its canonical verses along with brief framing notes—a structural feature of repetitive Jātaka stories noted by Naomi Appleton [Appleton 2010; Fausböll 1879].

In the verses, the Bodhisatta (a pigeon) observes a crane-like figure in the crow's nest; the commentary clarifies that the Bodhisatta is ironically addressing his friend the crow, who has been scalded and coated in white curds or buttermilk (*takkamakkhitasarīratā*) after attempting to steal human food [Fausböll 1879]. The Bodhisatta remarks that birds cannot safely enjoy human delicacies and subsequently flies away [Fausböll 1879]. At the conclusion of the teaching, the greedy monk realizes the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), and the Buddha reveals that the crow was the monk in a past life, while he himself was the pigeon [Fausböll 1879].

SuttaCentral lists no canonical parallels for this Jātaka in other languages, noting four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus confirms Pali-internal text reuse consisting of four segments (608 characters) shared directly with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match spanning segments §1.2–3.4 to commentary lines §2397–2404), with no significant cross-language alignments detected [DharmaNexus].
